note: PARAPHRASED summaries of NIST AI RMF 1.0 subcategories (a 24-item subset), not the official text. Verify wording at the NIST AI Resource Center. Not an official NIST product.

subcategories.title: Legal and regulatory requirements
subcategories.summary: Legal and regulatory requirements that apply to AI are identified, understood, managed and documented.

subcategories.title: AI system inventory
subcategories.summary: Mechanisms exist to keep an inventory of AI systems, prioritised by risk.

subcategories.title: Roles and responsibilities
subcategories.summary: Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication for AI risk are documented and clear to staff.

subcategories.title: Training
subcategories.summary: Staff and partners receive AI risk management training suited to their duties.

subcategories.title: Human oversight roles
subcategories.summary: Policies define the roles of humans in overseeing AI systems and in human-AI configurations.

subcategories.title: Impact documentation
subcategories.summary: Teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI they design, develop or deploy.

subcategories.title: Third-party risk policy
subcategories.summary: Policies address risks from third-party AI software, data and intellectual property.

subcategories.title: Intended purpose and context
subcategories.summary: The intended purpose, context of use, users and applicable laws for each AI system are documented.

subcategories.title: Knowledge limits
subcategories.summary: Known limits of the system and how humans should use and oversee its output are documented.

subcategories.title: Human oversight processes
subcategories.summary: Processes for human oversight of the AI system are defined and assigned.

subcategories.title: Third-party components
subcategories.summary: Legal and other risks of third-party components in the AI system are mapped.

subcategories.title: Impact likelihood and magnitude
subcategories.summary: The likelihood and magnitude of each identified positive and negative impact are assessed.

subcategories.title: Metrics selected
subcategories.summary: Metrics and methods for measuring AI risks are chosen, and any risks left unmeasured are documented.

subcategories.title: Independent assessment
subcategories.summary: Assessors independent of the development team take part in evaluating the system.

subcategories.title: Production monitoring
subcategories.summary: System behaviour is monitored while in production.

subcategories.title: Validity and reliability
subcategories.summary: The system is shown to be valid and reliable, with limits of generalisation documented.

subcategories.title: Security and resilience
subcategories.summary: Security and resilience of the system are evaluated and documented.

subcategories.title: Privacy risk
subcategories.summary: Privacy risk of the system is examined and documented.

subcategories.title: Fairness and bias
subcategories.summary: Fairness and bias are evaluated and results documented.

subcategories.title: End-user feedback
subcategories.summary: Channels let end users and affected people report problems and appeal outcomes.

subcategories.title: Residual risk
subcategories.summary: Risks that remain after treatment are documented and communicated to those affected.

subcategories.title: Disengagement
subcategories.summary: Mechanisms exist to supersede, disengage or deactivate a system that behaves outside its intended use.

subcategories.title: Post-deployment monitoring plan
subcategories.summary: Post-deployment monitoring plans exist, covering user input, appeal and override, change management and decommissioning.

subcategories.title: Incident communication
subcategories.summary: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant parties and affected communities, and response and recovery are tracked.
